fieldMarks: Small: 5-10.2 cm; rusty or gray-brown with grayish sides and black and bluish speckles.
Four toes on each hind foot.
Constricted ring at the base of the tail.
13-14 costal grooves; tail about 57% of length.
Females have rounded snouts, breeding males squared snouts.
behavior: Relatively sedentary, moving short distances between breeding sites and nonbreeding habitat; mostly inactive in the coldest months.
If disturbed curls up with head under the tail, or may detach its tail.
Nests communally in moss or protected sites above or beside a pool, females guarding the eggs about 2 months.
habitat: Swamps, boggy streams and wet wooded or open areas near quiet mossy or sedgy pools; Sphagnum moss is commonly abundant.
range: Discontinuously from Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, southern Quebec and southern Ontario through Michigan, Wisconsin and Minnesota south to southeastern Oklahoma, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, the Florida panhandle and Georgia; fairly continuous in the northeast, spotty in the southwest.

lookalikes.name: Southern two-lined salamander
lookalikes.howToTell: Five toes on each hind foot and no tail constriction.
